entries.example: A plant cell, labelled - wall outside, membrane inside it, then nucleus, chloroplast and the large vacuole: the full plant kit.
entries.meaning: The smallest unit of life; every living thing is made of one or more cells, each carrying the structures it needs to stay alive.

entries.example: A plant cell, labelled - wall outside, membrane inside it, then nucleus, chloroplast and the large vacuole: the full plant kit.
entries.meaning: A tough outer layer found in plant cells only. It gives the cell its shape and strength but is fully permeable.

entries.example: The membrane is the gatekeeper - food crosses in, waste crosses out, and a harmful particle is refused: the membrane chooses.
entries.meaning: The thin layer around every cell that controls what enters and leaves. It is selectively permeable.

entries.example: The membrane is the gatekeeper - food crosses in, waste crosses out, and a harmful particle is refused: the membrane chooses.
entries.meaning: Letting some substances through while keeping others out - the membrane chooses, like a gatekeeper.

entries.example: Two specialists: nucleus and chloroplast - the nucleus controls the cell with its instructions, the chloroplast traps light to make food.
entries.meaning: The control centre of the cell, holding the instructions that run everything the cell does.

entries.example: Two specialists: nucleus and chloroplast - the nucleus controls the cell with its instructions, the chloroplast traps light to make food.
entries.meaning: The plant-only structure that traps light energy to make food by photosynthesis.

entries.example: Why plants stand up straight - a full vacuole pushes the membrane against the wall so the cell is turgid; lose water and it goes flaccid.
entries.meaning: A fluid-filled space. In plant cells it is large and permanent; filled with water it pushes the cell firm.

entries.example: An animal cell, labelled - membrane, nucleus and mitochondrion only: no wall, no chloroplast, no large vacuole.
entries.meaning: The structure that releases energy from food, in both plant and animal cells.

entries.example: Label the main structures of plant and animal cells and state each job
entries.meaning: The jelly-like substance inside the cell where most of its work happens.

entries.example: Why plants stand up straight - a full vacuole pushes the membrane against the wall so the cell is turgid; lose water and it goes flaccid.
entries.meaning: A plant cell swollen firm because its full vacuole pushes the membrane against the wall.

entries.example: Cells team up: the organisation ladder - cell to tissue to organ to system, as in leaf cell to leaf tissue to leaf to shoot system.
entries.meaning: A group of similar cells working together at the same job, such as leaf tissue.

entries.example: Cells team up: the organisation ladder - cell to tissue to organ to system, as in leaf cell to leaf tissue to leaf to shoot system.
entries.meaning: A structure made of several tissues working together, such as a leaf or a heart.

entries.example: Cells team up: the organisation ladder - cell to tissue to organ to system, as in leaf cell to leaf tissue to leaf to shoot system.
entries.meaning: A group of organs working together, such as the shoot system or the circulatory system.
